name: start_audit_session
description:
Audit the calling MCP agent. Heron asks 9+ compliance questions about what the agent does, what data it touches, and what permissions it holds. The response includes a `status` field that tells the caller which interview mode is active:
- `interviewing`: the client declared MCP sampling capability. Heron will ask each question via sampling/createMessage in the background. The caller can poll progress via get_report or watch the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3700/dashboard/sessions/<id>.
- `awaiting_answer`: the client does not support sampling (e.g. Codex CLI / Codex.app). The response includes the first question under `next_question`. The caller MUST reply by calling submit_answer with the returned session_id plus an answer string. Each submit_answer returns either the next question (status=awaiting_answer) or the final report (status=complete).

agent_name.description: Optional human-readable name for the audited agent.

name: submit_answer
description: Provide the next answer to an in-progress Heron audit interview started via start_audit_session. Returns either the next question (status=awaiting_answer) or the final report (status=complete) once all questions have been answered. Always pair with start_audit_session — this tool is only callable when an audit session is in the 'awaiting_answer' state (non-sampling clients, AAP-55).

session_id.description: The session id returned by a prior start_audit_session call.

answer.description: The agent’s answer to the most recently asked question.

name: start_verification
description:
Scan agent's runtime environment for evidence supporting the audit transcript.

Reads (only for the runtime under audit):
  - MCP server configurations from the runtime config (e.g. ~/.codex/config.toml)
  - Plugin / skill / auth credential NAMES (never values)
  - Environment variable NAMES from workspace .env files

NEVER reads:
  - Actual credential values, tokens, passwords
  - Other runtimes' config directories (e.g. when auditing Codex, ~/.claude/* is not touched)
  - Files outside the standard discovery paths

Output: deterministic evidence to verify the agent's declared scope.

session_id.description: The session id returned by a prior start_audit_session call. Must reference a session whose interview has completed (status complete). Sessions in analysis_failed are rejected: re-run start_audit_session first.

runtime.description: The runtime under audit. Discovery reads only this runtime's evidence directories — when auditing Codex, only ~/.codex/* is scanned; ~/.claude/* is not touched.

workspace_hint.description: Optional absolute workspace path the verification scan should target. When omitted, Heron uses the workspace path the MCP client advertised at session start, falling back to the server process cwd.

name: report_mcp_tools_list
description:
Forward the raw `tools/list` response from one of your MCP servers to Heron.

Heron will:
  - Parse the response to extract tool names + descriptions
  - Run the same read/write classification as stdio servers (AAP-75)
  - Merge into the discovery report alongside stdio results

NEVER:
  - Stores the credentials you used to call the server
  - Asks for or sees those credentials

session_id.description: The session id returned by a prior start_audit_session call. The forwarded inventory is attached to this audit run.

server_name.description: The MCP server name as you declared it in your systems_enum answer (Q2). Used to deduplicate forwards: a second report for the same server replaces the first.

raw_response.description: The verbatim JSON-RPC `tools/list` response body your MCP server returned. Heron accepts the full envelope `{ jsonrpc, id, result: { tools } }`, the result-only blob `{ result: { tools } }`, or a bare `{ tools }` body.

name: report_oauth_scopes
description:
Forward your OAuth provider's token-introspection response to Heron so it can verify your GRANTED scopes deterministically.

For each OAuth provider you use (Google Workspace, etc.):
  1. Call the provider's introspection endpoint with YOUR access token.
     Google: GET https://oauth2.googleapis.com/tokeninfo?access_token=<your-token>
  2. Forward the RAW introspection response here (it contains the granted `scope` field). Do NOT send the token itself — only the introspection response.

Heron will:
  - Parse the granted scopes from the response
  - Diff them against your declared usage to surface over-broad grants

NEVER:
  - Reads, stores, or asks for your access/refresh token — only the introspection response

If the introspection call fails (token expired/invalid), forward the error response anyway — Heron records an honest "introspection attempted" state.

session_id.description: The session id returned by a prior start_audit_session call. The forwarded scopes are attached to this audit run.

provider.description: The OAuth provider you introspected, e.g. "google-workspace". Used to deduplicate forwards: a second report for the same provider replaces the first.

raw_response.description: The verbatim introspection response body your OAuth provider returned (for Google, the tokeninfo JSON with the `scope` field). Heron parses the granted scopes from it. This is the introspection RESPONSE, never the token.

name: get_report
description: Retrieve a previously-generated Heron audit report by its id.

report_id.description: The session id returned by a prior start_audit_session call.

name: compare_reports
description: Compare two Heron audit reports by id and return a markdown diff highlighting what was resolved, what changed, and what was added between the two audits.
